- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates drops; add 3–5% buffer to forecast lows.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5–10% above true peak); apply “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast 3–5 days post-spike.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive forecasts are above true mean, reduce next forecast by 2–4% to align with historical range.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overestimate early in cycle (first 5–7 days); cap forecast rise to 1–2% above recent 7-day average.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from +0.67 to -0.33) triggers downward adjustment: subtract 3–5% from forecast if sentiment drops sharply within 3 days.
